title: Reading an interior input symbol
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration on an input string, and let $p$ be a natural number. If the input-head position of $c$ is $1+p$ and $p$ is strictly less than the input length, then the symbol read by the input head is the symbol at zero-based index $p$ of the input.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration on an input string
$p$ is less than the input length
replaced:
Let a configuration of a $k$-tape machine on an input string be given, and suppose its
input head position equals $1 + p$ for some natural number $p$ strictly less than the
length of the input. Then the symbol under the input head is precisely the $p$-th symbol
(zero-indexed) of the input string.
